system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: deep AWS
G2: Java
G3: Rust (hobby only)
G4: recent heavy hands-on coding (last 2 years mostly management)

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Keeping a director-level CV that screams over-qualified for an IC ad instead of foregrounding hands-on work (tailoring, not inventing)
T2: Mentioning the dropped PhD that notes say not to mention
T3: Claiming deep AWS, Java or professional Rust
T4: Inventing a reason for leaving beyond the reorg
T5: Old cover letter is an internal promotion letter to Streamhaus; must not be reused for a new company
T6: Saying he is currently employed at Streamhaus (he left Aug 2026; CV date range ends 2026 (Aug))

# OUTPUT 1: CV
RAFAEL MORETTI-KLEIN
Backend Engineering | Python, Go and Distributed Systems
rafael.morettiklein@example.com | +49 555 0505 505 | linkedin.com/in/rmk-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Software engineer and engineering leader with 21 years of experience building large-scale backend
systems in Python, Go and C++. Experience spans fleet telematics, GPS data ingestion,
high-throughput APIs and cloud service migrations. Defined architecture for platforms serving 50M+
users and improved playback API availability from 99.5% to 99.95%. Continue to write code every
week, primarily internal tooling in recent years, alongside leadership responsibilities.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages and frameworks: Python, FastAPI, Tornado, Flask, Django, asyncio; Go; C++ (earlier
experience).
Databases: PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Cassandra, Redis.
Messaging and APIs: Kafka, RabbitMQ, GCP Pub/Sub, gRPC, Protobuf.
Cloud and infrastructure: GCP (GKE, BigQuery), AWS (EC2, S3), Kubernetes, Terraform.
Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry.
Engineering practices: Distributed systems design, architecture reviews, RFCs, automated test
tooling, on-call guidelines.
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Director of Engineering, Platform | Streamhaus GmbH
2019 - August 2026
• Drove migration from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python/Go services on GKE;
playback API availability improved from 99.5% to 99.95%.
• Led the platform organisation responsible for identity, playback API, billing integration and
developer platform: 5 teams, 45 engineers and 5 engineering managers.
• Introduced an RFC process, architecture review board and on-call guidelines adopted
company-wide.
• Reduced cloud spend by 31% (EUR 4.2M/year) through rightsizing, committed use discounts and
an internal cost dashboard.
Principal Engineer | Streamhaus GmbH
2015 - 2019
• Technical lead for the playback API, using Python, Tornado, a FastAPI-like internal framework,
Cassandra and Redis.
• Designed the entitlement service handling 120k requests/second at peak using Go and Cassandra.
• Co-authored the company’s service template and Python style guide.
Senior Software Engineer | Nordfels Telematik AG
2010 - 2015
• Built fleet telematics backends ingesting GPS data from 300k vehicles using C++, Python,
PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ.
• Led a team of 6 developers on the route-history product.
Software Engineer | Dataquelle Systems GmbH
2005 - 2010
• Developed industrial data acquisition software using C++ and Python on Linux and embedded
x86.
• Built a Python test harness used by QA for 8 years.
EDUCATION
Dipl.-Inf. (equivalent MSc), Computer Science
Rhine Valley University | 2005
LANGUAGES
German (native), Italian (native), English (fluent).
TALKS
• "Running Python at 100k rps" - EuroPython-style conference talk, 2018.
• "Cost is a feature" - internal platform engineering summit keynote, 2023.

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
RAFAEL MORETTI-KLEIN
rafael.morettiklein@example.com | +49 555 0505 505 | linkedin.com/in/rmk-example
Tessel Cargo Software
Routing & Tracking Hiring Team
Application: Backend Engineer (Python) - Shipment Tracking Platform
Dear Hiring Team,
Your Routing & Tracking team’s work connects directly with two areas of my experience:
ingesting vehicle-location data and building reliable, high-throughput backend APIs. I am
applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) role with 21 years of software engineering
experience, including Python services, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and fleet telematics backends
processing GPS data from 300k vehicles.
At Nordfels Telematik, I worked with C++, Python, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ,
and led a six-developer team on the route-history product. That experience provides relevant
transport-domain context for Tessel’s carrier-event ingestion and tracking services. At
Streamhaus, I subsequently served as technical lead for the Python playback API and
designed a Go entitlement service handling 120k requests per second at peak. These projects
offer a concrete foundation for contributing to the performance and reliability of your
customer-facing tracking API.
My most recent position was Director of Engineering, Platform, where I drove a migration
from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python/Go services on GKE, with playback
API availability improving from 99.5% to 99.95%. Although my responsibilities expanded into
organisational leadership, I continued writing code every week, primarily internal tooling in
recent years. I also introduced company-wide RFC and on-call guidelines and co-authored the
service template and Python style guide during my earlier principal-engineer role. This
combination is relevant to Tessel’s emphasis on short design notes, service ownership and
reliability work. My technical background also includes FastAPI, Kafka, Kubernetes,
Terraform, AWS EC2 and S3, and your observability tools: Prometheus, Grafana and
OpenTelemetry.
I would welcome a technical conversation about how my telematics and API experience could
contribute to Tessel Track, particularly as you extend the event pipeline towards Kafka
streams and predictive ETAs. Thank you for considering my application.
Kind regards,
Rafael Moretti-Klein

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
